name: Keir Starmer
role: UK prime minister (2024-2026); Labour leader (2020-2026); Director of Public Prosecutions (2008-2013)
summary: Starmer is a former human rights barrister and Director of Public Prosecutions who led Labour from 2020, won the 2024 general election and resigned as prime minister in July 2026. His government paired a pro-growth, pro-investment agenda (planning reform, nuclear and clean power, a National Wealth Fund) with public ownership of rail and a state energy company, stronger employment rights, an NHS kept publicly funded but reformed, tighter immigration, higher defence spending and close ties to NATO and Europe.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Called the NHS 'a public service, publicly funded, free at the point of use' and ruled out abandoning that principle in his reform speech.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: His government raised the National Minimum Wage by record amounts (6.7% in Oct 2024) and again later, and he cites it as an achievement; no stated aim of a large 'substantial' rise beyond that.

public-ownership.rationale: Manifesto he led brought rail operators into public ownership, created publicly owned Great British Energy and allowed municipal bus ownership; other utilities such as water stayed privately owned, with tougher regulation.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Ended non-dom status and VAT exemption for private schools and raised taxes on 'broader shoulders', but his 2020 pledge to raise income tax on the top 5% was dropped and the manifesto ruled out rises in income tax, National Insurance and VAT for working people.

unions-good.rationale: Manifesto promised to strengthen workers' collective voice including through trade unions; the Employment Rights Act repealed most anti-union legislation of 2016 and 2023. He did not frame this in terms of unions being good for society in general.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Mixed record: tougher regulation of water, energy suppliers, gambling and online platforms, but also a stated drive to strip out 'needless regulation' and 'pointless gold-plating' to speed investment.

cut-welfare.rationale: Scrapped the two-child limit and raised the Universal Credit standard rate, yet described the welfare system as trapping people in worklessness and reduced the health element of UC for some claimants and means-tested Winter Fuel Payments.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Manifesto committed to making all existing strands of hate crime aggravated offences and to tackling antisemitic and Islamophobic hate; he called for rejecting hate in all forms. This concerns hate crime law rather than speech bans as such.

state-harmful.rationale: Explicitly wants a 'more dynamic, more decisive' state and uses government to drive investment, health and policing; the opposite of the claim.

empower-police-military.rationale: Brought defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2027 with an ambition of 3%, and promised 13,000 more neighbourhood police; manifesto also created a Border Security Command with counter-terror style powers.

decide-locally.rationale: Manifesto pledged devolution of power across England and powers for mayors and local leaders; Plan for Change speech wants a state less hostile to devolution. He also centralises through national missions, so not strong.

rehabilitation.rationale: Manifesto says prisons should not be 'academies of crime' and aims to cut reoffending, but also stresses punishment of criminals, and his government used early release to relieve overcrowding.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Supported Black Lives Matter and promised a Race Equality Act as a defining cause; manifesto repeated the commitment.

reduce-immigration.rationale: 'I believe we need to reduce immigration significantly'; white paper tightens work, family and study routes.

free-trade.rationale: Said there is no credible economic vision that does not position Britain as an open trading economy, and struck trade deals with the US, India and the EU; opposed tariffs on allies.

nation-first.rationale: Says he always acts in the national interest but argues turning inward surrenders control and puts weight on alliances (NATO, E3, EU reset, Berlin treaty).

open-borders.rationale: Condemned a 'one-nation experiment in open borders' and says the new system must be controlled, selective and fair.

limit-growth.rationale: Calls growth the number one mission of his government.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: At COP29 said there is no security without climate security, set a clean power by 2030 goal, an 81% cut by 2035 target, closed the last coal plant; frames action as growth opportunity.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Funded Sizewell C and accepted the Fingleton review, saying Britain is the most expensive place to build nuclear power and regulation must change.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Called tariffs against allies 'completely wrong' and a trade war in no one's interest; stresses open trade. (Used emergency powers to save British Steel, which is not a tariff measure.)

state-directs-investment.rationale: Created the National Wealth Fund and Great British Energy, and said government must shape AI and industrial strategy rather than leave it to the market.

political-violence-never.rationale: Said after the attempt on Trump that political violence in any form has no place in societies; condemns rioters and Hamas terrorism.

military-superiority.rationale: Says Britain must build hard power to deter, but no stated goal of superiority over rivals.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Celebrates Britain as a diverse nation and says people who look different living together peacefully is what makes it strong.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Wants to 'turbocharge' AI adoption and remove barriers, but also safety institutes and public-service framing.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Uses AI to speed planning, job centre forms and social work paperwork, but frames it as freeing people for human work, not taking over decisions.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Mission-led government with milestones to be 'fairly judged'; rejects drift and focuses on delivery.

direct-action.rationale: Proscribed Palestine Action and told rioters they would face the full force of the law; works through Parliament.

taxation-theft.rationale: Defends tax rises as fair, necessary choices for public services and pursues tax avoidance.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Says 'we do not seek conflict', stresses rule of law and respect for sovereignty (Greenland, Ukraine).

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Says Britain recognised Israel as a homeland for the Jewish people and seeks a safe and secure Israel alongside a Palestinian state.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Rejected 'rolling the dice with extra borrowing' and 'reckless borrowing', holds non-negotiable fiscal rules; but also says austerity scarred productivity and backs public investment.

national-self-determination.rationale: Recognised Palestinian statehood and said Greenland's future belongs to its people.

class-collaboration.rationale: Manifesto proposes partnership between government, business and trade unions.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Career and platform centre on race equality (Stephen Lawrence prosecution as DPP, Race Equality Act promise).

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: No new North Sea oil and gas licences; closed the last coal power plant; ended the onshore wind ban.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Asks for integration and learning English but says 'I celebrate' diversity; does not ask migrants to give up their culture.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Government does far more than defence, justice and property protection (NHS, welfare, industrial policy).

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Human rights barrister; manifesto commits to remaining in the ECHR and anti-discrimination protections.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Scrapped the two-child limit and made child poverty a priority, but did not frame all institutions around the poor first.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Employment Rights Act repeals the Minimum Service Levels Act and most of the Trade Union Act 2016 (which included the strike ballot thresholds).

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Says diversity makes Britain strong; blames lack of fair rules, not diversity, for the risk of an 'island of strangers'.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: White paper extends the time to settled status from five to ten years.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Backed Remain and wants a closer EU relationship and alignment, but ruled out rejoining the single market or customs union.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Calls NATO commitment profound, applies Article 5 and keeps forces abroad.

death-penalty.rationale: Spent years doing pro bono work against death sentences in Africa and the Caribbean and sat on the FCDO's Death Penalty Advisory Panel.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Manifesto pledged return to 0.7%, but his government cut aid from 0.5% to 0.3% to fund defence, saying he was unhappy to do so.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Manifesto: commitment to the UK's nuclear deterrent is 'absolute'; Munich speech speaks of coordinating it with France.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Manifesto commits to an independent Bank of England targeting 2% inflation.

collective-defense.rationale: Said Britain's commitment to Article 5 is 'as profound now as ever' and that the UK would come to allies' aid.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Made 'no annexations in the West Bank' a condition of Palestine recognition and backs Ukraine against occupation.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Manifesto: hereditary peers remain 'indefensible' and would lose their seats; the monarchy was not challenged.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Manifesto and government strengthen anti-discrimination and employment protections; calls conversion practices abuse.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Government banned hen cages and farrowing crates; manifesto promises to ban trail hunting and puppy farming.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Manifesto: Britain will unequivocally remain in the ECHR and values international law; he stresses commitment to international law.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Manifesto uses spare independent-sector capacity to cut NHS waiting lists inside a publicly funded NHS.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Manifesto promises LGBT+ protections and a ban on conversion practices.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Manifesto pledged to modernise gender recognition law while keeping a diagnosis; later ruled out self-identification and said trans women should not use women-only spaces.

assisted-dying.rationale: Voted Aye on the Terminally Ill Adults Bill at second and third readings (free vote) after pledging Parliament would have a vote.

social-market-economy.rationale: Pairs pro-investment, pro-business growth agenda with employment rights, welfare and regulation.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Increasing defence spending; says strength deters aggression.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Leading NATO ally; commits to NATO first.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Promises more neighbourhood police and added prison capacity.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Keeps the Trident deterrent based in Britain and bought F-35A aircraft for NATO's nuclear mission.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Defends NHS in public hands, nationalised rail operating contracts and allowed municipal bus ownership; water stays private but is more tightly regulated.

second-chamber.rationale: Manifesto: replace the House of Lords with an alternative, more representative second chamber.

free-public-college.rationale: His government raised tuition fees; he abandoned his 2020 pledge to abolish them.

future-generations.rationale: Wrote that there are precious things in our environment to 'protect, preserve and pass on to future generations'.

arms-reduction.rationale: Raising defence spending to 2.5% then 3% of GDP, citing grave threats; says Britain does not seek conflict.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Manifesto: strengthen workers' collective voice through unions; government reversed anti-union laws.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Manifesto: fiscal rules are 'non-negotiable'; strengthened OBR scrutiny. Whether legally binding is not stated.

public-service-media.rationale: Named the BBC among precious institutions and manifesto promises constructive work with public service broadcasters.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Absolute commitment to the deterrent; no unilateral disarmament.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: White paper requires English language across all routes including dependants.

close-ties-china.rationale: Seeks a 'consistent, durable, respectful' relationship and visited China in 2026, while anchoring policy on the US and Europe.

notes: His positions moved considerably after winning the 2020 leadership on a left-leaning ten-pledge platform (higher income tax on the top 5%, abolishing tuition fees, freedom of movement); the most recent government record is used throughout. Answers are limited to his speeches, manifesto, votes and government record; where evidence was mixed or absent they are 0 or null. The gov.uk transcripts carry some 'political content redacted' markers.
